material.name: CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA)
material.form: additively manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM)
material.initial_state: face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution with epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides

intervention.description: Mechanical testing across temperature ranges to evaluate properties and deformation behaviors

structure.description: Fine grains, high dislocation density, and fine precipitates

evidence_units.mechanism: Outstanding mechanical properties achieved through fine grains, high dislocation density, and fine precipitates
evidence_spans: The microstructure, temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation behaviors of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) additively manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM) were investigated.
SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides.

Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present.

The excellent mechanical properties of SLM-built HEA were achieved with fine grains, high dislocation density and fine precipitates at low temperatures (25 °C to 600 °C), and by high dislocation density and fine precipitates at high temperatures (700 °C or higher).

intervention.action: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) with optimal process conditions
intervention.description: Manufacturing using optimal SLM process parameters to deduce microstructure

structure.description: FCC single phase with epitaxial growth grains, cellular and columnar substructures, and nano-sized precipitates
microstructure: Epitaxial growth grains perpendicular to building direction (BD)
Cellular and columnar structures (~400 nm size)
Mn2O3 oxide precipitates at cell boundaries (average size 27.3 nm)

evidence_units.mechanism: Thermal contraction strain during rapid solidification and cooling causes dislocation formation; dislocation networks form to compensate for distortions from thermal contraction stress; Mn2O3 precipitates form specifically due to SLM conditions preventing Cr-Mn oxide or sigma-phase formation; heat dissipation direction dictates grain growth and texture development (epitaxial growth and <001>/<101>/<111> textures).

outcome.measurement_method: Compressive yield strength at room temperature

evidence_spans: Figure 1 shows an SEM-BSE image and EDS mapping results of as-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. The BSE image revealed some micron-scale gas pores, but coarse defects or cracks were not observed in the as-built HEA (Porosity: 0.13%).
limitations: Dislocation density higher than homogenized HEA [33]

intervention.description: Room- and high-temperature compressive stress-strain testing

structure.description: Microstructure evolved from work hardening with slip and deformation twinning to dynamic recrystallization (DRX) and dynamic recovery (DRV)
microstructure: Deformation twins (DTs) at room temperature, 500 °C, and 600 °C
Fine grains (hundreds of nm to few μm) at 700 °C and higher
Recrystallized and substructured regions at 700 °C and higher

evidence_units.mechanism: At temperatures up to 600 °C, deformation occurs via slip and deformation twinning; at temperatures higher than 700 °C, yield strength drop and work softening are attributed to microstructure evolution via dynamic recrystallization (DRX) and dynamic recovery (DRV).
evidence_spans: SLM-built HEA showed a general tendency of decreasing strength as the compressive temperature increased. However, the yield strength for each temperature (Fig. 6b ) decreased as temperature increased, but the decrease up to 700 °C was significantly smaller.

material.name: CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy
material.composition: equiatomic (Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, Ni ~20 at. %)

intervention.description: Analysis of serrated flow and activation energy during deformation

structure.description: Deformed microstructure exhibiting type-C serration behavior

evidence_units.mechanism: Type-C serration at 600 °C is caused by the unlocking of aged dislocations; activation energy analysis (335 kJ/mol) indicates the mechanism is related to cooperative lattice diffusion of constituent elements rather than interstitial solute atoms, with additional influence from nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates.
evidence_spans: Activation energy measured 335 kJ/mol, which was significantly higher than the activation energy related to the diffusion of common interstitial solutes (76–103 kJ/mol [67] ). This was also similar to or higher than the activation energies for the self-diffusion of Co, Cr, Fe, Mn and Ni, which are 270, 313, 309, 272 and 304 kJ/mol, respectively. In other words, the serrated flow of SLM-built HEA can be uninfluenced by interstitial atoms, and this is related to the cooperative lattice diffusion of constituent elements. In addition, the reason why the activation energy is higher than the self-diffusion activation energies of elements is suspected to be due to nano-sized Mn 2 O 3 , which can cause a serrated flow, also having an influence on deformation.

material.name: CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy
material.initial_state: random solid solution FCC single phase, epitaxial growth grains, cellular and columnar structures composed of dislocation networks, Mn2O3 of 27.3 nm at the interface

structure.description: cellular and columnar structure composed of dislocation networks and nano-sized oxides, Mn2O3 at the cellular structure boundary and grain boundary

evidence_units.mechanism: Zener drag effect caused by nano-sized oxides (Mn2O3) and migrated grain boundaries delays full recrystallization, reducing the overall pressure for recrystallization and delaying strain softening

comparison.baseline_material: SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA (theoretical expectation without drag)

evidence_spans: On the other hand, the reason why a dramatic decrease in flow stress did not occur in SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA deformations up to 900 °C is suspected to be due to full recrystallization not occurring easily.
This is suspected to be a result of the Zener drag effect [72] caused by the oxides formed at the cellular structure boundary and grain boundary, which delay RX as a result.
As SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA has a high fraction F v and d of 27.3 nm, P Z increases significantly.
Therefore, the overall pressure for RX decreases dramatically.
In addition, the migrated grain boundary formed during gDRX is also a factor that delays RX.

Therefore, while P D is identical, the overall pressure for recrystallization decreases as a result of the Zener pinning pressure ( P Z ) caused by Mn 2 O 3 and further retarding pressure ( P C ) caused by the migrated grain boundary.
As RX is delayed due to this, SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA is expected to delay strain softening up to 900 °C.

structure.description: deformed samples had a clear cellular and columnar structure composed of dislocation networks as well as nano-sized oxides, ultra-fine grains with an average size of 378 nm were found at grain boundaries, migration of HABs observed

evidence_units.mechanism: DRX is caused by combination of dDRX and gDRX, following the process of i) accumulation of dislocations at HABs, ii) migration or bulging of HABs, and iii) rotation of HABs; gDRX is characterized by flow stress continuously decreasing by small amounts

outcome.measurement_method: ECC images, HR-EBSD analysis, true stress-strain curve

evidence_spans: In the range of temperatures above 700 °C, the deformed samples had a clear cellular and columnar structure composed of dislocation networks as well as nano-sized oxides, and this confirmed that the slip and partial RX observed in EBSD are the main deformation mechanisms.
In order to analyze the DRX phenomenon, HR-EBSD analysis was performed on the sample deformed at 700 °C (Fig. 12 ).
In the IPF map, ultra-fine grains with an average size of 378 nm were found at grain boundaries.
On the other hand, the migration of HABs was observed in grain boundaries with no ultra-fine grains (white arrow).

In the GND distribution map, the dislocations in DRXed grains confirmed that they are not new, strain-free grains (i.e., the main RX mechanism in dDRX), and it is possible to expected that ultra-fine grains are formed due to the rotation of HABs.

In other words, the DRX of SLM-built HEA is caused by combination of dDRX and gDRX, which follow the process of i) accumulation of dislocations at HABs, ii) migration or bulging of HABs, and iii) rotation of HABs.

As seen in the curve, gDRX, where flow stress continuously decreases by small amounts, is somewhat different with dDRX, where flow stress decreases sharply, and cDRX, where saturation occurs (See Fig. S4).

evidence_units.mechanism: σ-phase formation at cell structure boundary
evidence_spans: In the case of the sample deformed at 900 °C, σ-phase was formed at the cell structure boundary.

intervention.description: deformation in relatively low temperature conditions (~600 °C)

structure.description: large number of DT bundles identified, substructure maintained due to dislocation climb

evidence_units.mechanism: Dislocation density increase and DT evolution suppress dislocation, causing work hardening; slip and DT evolution are main deformation mechanisms

outcome.direction: greater than annealed and hot-rolled equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs

comparison.baseline_material: annealed and hot-rolled equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs

evidence_spans: In relatively low temperature conditions (~600 °C), σ m , σ k , σ ρ and σ Or contribute to achieving mechanical properties greater than those of annealed and hot-rolled equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs.

In the range of temperatures above 700 °C, the deformed samples had a clear cellular and columnar structure composed of dislocation networks as well as nano-sized oxides, and this confirmed that the slip and partial RX observed in EBSD are the main deformation mechanisms.
In contrast, above 700 °C, the substructure is maintained due to dislocation climb, and yield strength drop and work softening are suspected to occur due to partial RX.
In addition, the reason why work hardening occurs at temperatures below 600 °C is suspected to be because dislocation is suppressed as a result of dislocation density increase and DT evolution.
Compressive deformation microstructure observation confirmed that slip and DT were the dominant behaviors from room temperature to 600 °C

evidence_spans: The above powders were then used as feedstocks for SLM processing (model: Concept Laser Mlab cusing) under high-purity Ar gas to minimize oxidation.
A laser scanning speed of 600 mm/s was applied to fabricate bar-type specimens with dimensions of 85 mm × 10 m × 10 m.
A hatch space of 80 µm with a laser power of 90 W was applied.
The layer thickness was set to 25 µm.
In addition, a scanning pattern of 180° angle rotation for the two consecutive layers was applied.

material.name: equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA
material.initial_state: SLM-built, prepared by electrical discharge machining, size Φ 4 mm × height 6 mm

intervention.description: Temperature-dependent mechanical property evaluation via compression tests

evidence_units.mechanism: Compression testing at varying temperatures evaluates temperature-dependent mechanical properties
evidence_spans: To evaluate the temperature-dependent mechanical properties of SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, a cylindrical specimen with a size of Φ 4 mm × height 6 mm was prepared by using electrical discharge machining according to scanning direction (SD).
Compression tests were performed using MTS-810 equipment at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C.
An initial strain rate of 1 × 10 −3 −1 and an engineering strain limit of 0.4 were applied.
Before the temperature-dependent compressive tests, the SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs were preheated in an electric resistance furnace at a heating rate of 10 °C/min.
The compression tests were conducted three times for each condition.
Furthermore, MoS 2 spray used as a lubricant to reduce physical friction.
